messages:
emily.sales: Quick help pls — demo tomorrow. Customer sent a single JSON with ~5.8MB of plain text in the prompt and our API returns 413. Any low-effort unblock? @chris.eng
chris.eng: 413 = gateway rejecting the payload. Fast options: gzip the request, use chunked uploads, or presign the large doc and pass a short URL in the prompt. Which environment are they hitting?
laura.poc: They're on hosted in us-central. Tried gzip but client library didn't set Content-Encoding correctly. Can we force accept-encoding on the gateway?
dan.ops: We can accept compressed bodies, but client must send Content-Encoding: gzip. If they can't change client, infra can temporarily increase client_max_body_size for their account. @infra-bot please standby.
sec-bot: Note: presigned uploads are encrypted at rest and logged. For demos we can set short retention (24h) per request. If they need proof of deletion, we need a Security Ops runbook signed.
infra-bot: Temp action: increased client_max_body_size to 16M for account "acme-demo" on us-central edge. Auto-revert in 4 hours. Please retest.
laura.poc: Retested — sending same JSON now succeeds. Stream begins and model returns tokens.
emily.sales: Great. Two follow-ups customers often ask: should we chunk or instruct them to compress? What's recommended for long-term?
chris.eng: For production, avoid single huge prompts. Strategies: 1) Upload docs and reference by short pointer. 2) Preprocess with extract+summarize to fit model token limits. 3) Use streaming + smaller per-request contexts. Add a simple Python chunker to the docs.
laura.poc: I'll add presign example and gzip snippet to the POC runbook, and note security TTL option.
emily.sales: Thanks team, marking POC unblocked and adding pricing note for Dedicated demo if they request higher throughput. Closing thread :white_check_mark:
